designSummary: Cohort of first eligible discharges, time to first injurious fall within 90 days, death as a competing event.
sampleSize: About 4,200 discharges per year of adults aged 70 and over leave the medical wards; two years give about 8,400 discharges from about 6,000 distinct patients. If 22 percent have a burden score of 3 or more and 6 percent have an injurious fall within 90 days, about 360 events are expected. With 360 events the study has 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a hazard ratio of about 1.43 for score 3 or more versus 0 to 2 (Schoenfeld approximation); a hazard ratio of 1.3 would need about 660 events, roughly four years of discharges. The estimate will be reported with its confidence interval rather than as a significance verdict.
primaryAnalysis: Cause-specific Cox model for the first injurious fall with death as a competing event, adjusted for 12 pre-specified covariates: age, sex, frailty score, number of regular medicines, dementia, prior fall admission in the past year, discharge destination, length of stay, area deprivation quintile and three indication groups. Robust standard errors; proportional hazards checked with scaled Schoenfeld residuals.
secondaryAnalysis: Fine-Gray subdistribution model as a sensitivity analysis for absolute risk; the same model for hip fracture and any fall-related contact; the new-user, active-comparator, 30-day window and negative control analyses named in the protocol.
missingData: Burden score and frailty score are derived for every discharge; discharge destination is missing for about 2 percent and is handled by multiple imputation with 20 imputations; people who move out of the region are censored at the last contact with the regional hospitals.
multiplicity: One primary contrast; secondary outcomes and sensitivity analyses are reported with confidence intervals and labelled as secondary, without formal adjustment.
software: R with the survival package; analysis code and the covariate list archived before data access.
overfittingGuards: Covariate set fixed before data access
About 30 events per covariate for the primary model
Statistical analysis plan registered on the hospital research transparency page before extraction
summary: Cause-specific Cox model; about 360 expected events give 80 percent power for a hazard ratio of about 1.43; smaller effects would need more years of data.
